newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU mergers and takeovers -- (UPDATED JULY 10).
newsitem.headline: EU mergers and takeovers -- (UPDATED JULY 10).

text.p: The following are additions and deletions to the list of takeovers, mergers and joint ventures being reviewed by the European Commission under the European Union's merger regulation (*). The Commission has a month to clear or start a detailed, four-month probe after a deal has been filed.
**ADDITIONS
-- None **DELETIONS
-- Deutsche Bank's property unit Deutsche Immobilien
Anlagegesellschaft and VEBA's VEBA Immobilien AG
proposed joint control of Deutschbau, a company which builds
houses for German federal employees (Cleared on June 23)
** ON-GOING ONE-MONTH REVIEWS
-- Purchase by Germany's Lear Corporation GmbH, offshoot of
the U.S. firm of the same name and producer of car seats
and interior components, of Keiper Car Seating GmbH, a producer
of complete seat systems in just-in-time sequence (Notified 19
June)
-- Siemens and Thomson-CSF proposal to put
their air traffic management activities into a joint venture
called Airsys ATM SAS (Notified June 17)
-- Proposal by Southern Energy Holding mbH, which belongs to
Southern Co, Viag AG and Preussen Elektra to
acquire joint control of Bewag, an utility servicing electricity
customers in Berlin (Notified June 11)
-- Proposal by Cable & Wireless and A.P. Moeller's
Maersk Data A/S to create a joint venture called Cable &
Wireless Nautec Ltd to provide communications for container
ships (Notified June 3)
-- Proposal by Compagnie Generale d'Entreprises Automobiles
and Energie-Versorgung Schwaben AG to acquire joint control of
German transport firm DEG-Verkehrs GmbH (Notified June 2)
** DETAILED REVIEWS
-- Proposed merger between Guinness Plc and Grand
Metropolitan Plc (Full probe opened June 20)
-- Proposed Nordic soft drinks joint venture of Coca-Cola
and Carlsberg A/S of Denmark. (Full probe
opened May 2).
-- Boeing Co proposed acquisition of McDonnell Douglas
. (Full probe opened March 19).
(*) Commission has exclusive EU competence in corporate
concentrations involving firms with a combined global turnover
of 5.0 billion ecus and EU turnover of 250 million ecus each. It
has the power to block, or force changes to, deals which create
or strengthen dominant positions in the EU whether or not the companies involved are European.
